facts.value: pre-registered protocol for fitting L(D)=E+B/D^beta over the six budget points (docs/lessons/scaling_fit_protocol.md, v1.1, frozen before the points run): Chinchilla recipe verbatim (Huber delta=1e-3, L-BFGS-B, 252-start grid, linear space); ACCEPT RMS<=0.05 / WEAK <=0.10 / FAIL else; U-shape (++--++), monotone drift (run>=4 all >0.01), endpoint same-sign patterns falsify the form regardless of RMS; LOO beta delta>0.15 is an imprecision flag not a falsifier; single-point tree = rerun once / investigate root cause / endpoint voids the curve. Quantity = aggregate val NLL at the final checkpoint on a fixed val set. fb's mix-composition hypothesis resolved: domain weights are identical at all six points (measured 0.3238/0.4962/0.0757/0.0495/0.0252/0.0177/0.0118), the schedule is interleaved (randperm per phase), and the within-domain pool IS shuffled before the val carve-out (train.py:1129, random.Random(Cfg.seed).shuffle, seed=42 in Cfg and persisted via vars(cfg), 2c7ccf4) -- every budget point eats a random prefix of the same shuffled cache, so composition is constant in expectation and D is the only systematic variable. v1.1 corrections (fb ruling): (a) v1.0's 'source-ordered prefix' concern was wrong -- it audited build_corpus.py but not train.py's tokenization-cache layer; the pod's train.py was 142 files behind HEAD with nothing to say so (de shipped pod_drift guard); (b) warmup = pure 1% of steps with floor 2, not max(20, 1%) -- floor 20 gave a 9.2x ratio across points (9.2% at 0.2b vs 1.0% at 3.24b), pure 1% gives 1.1x; the confound is the ratio differing across points, not absolute shortness; 2-step warmup risk is validated by a 6-min 0.2b smoke test before the floor is raised. Preconditions for the six runs: shared tokenization cache (same corpus snapshot + vocab_id), frozen corpus snapshot fingerprinted in PROVENANCE, horizon-matched warmup. Fitter: scripts/fit_scaling.py (selftest: noise-free recovery, noisy ACCEPT, pattern detection)
